main_body: Flat desert sand ground patch (4x3 tiles) with sparse speckles, seen from above; not a standing object
top_band: none; the column scan shows a uniform sand tone (L=182) with 1-row speckle dots (L=204 and L=156), no top/front structure because this is a ground surface
evidence: The kind is terrain (a ground tile), so the standing-object 3/4 contract does not apply. The scan shows a seamless, uniform sand field with small highlight and shadow flecks. It has no standing volume, no receding side faces, and no elevation-style drawing that could fail the contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours in total and a median of 4 per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours for the grass reference. Even the paving reference, the simpler of the two, has 7. The sand is one base tone (L=182) with a few isolated light and dark pixels, and the same 16px speckle motif repeats mechanically across the patch. Flat-fill coverage is 0% only because the speckles interrupt the field; there is no real tone variation, clumping, grain or dune shading. Next to the grass reference it looks thinner and flatter. There are no outlines, which is fine for ground.
